result.label: Own-price elasticity, 330ml can
result.rationale: Smallest, most impulse-driven format; set near the elastic end of the brief's -0.8 to -2.5 CPG range.
result.reference: Context only, not a fitted value. Published scanner-data studies report a wide spread of soft-drink own-price elasticities, with household scanner data tending to be more elastic (https://pure.psu.edu/en/publications/a-meta-analysis-of-us-food-demand-elasticities-to-detect-the-impa/). Observational elasticities can also differ from experimental ones (https://www.msi.org/working-paper/observational-price-variation-in-scanner-data-cannot-reproduce-experimental-price-elasticities/), so the value carries a range that drives the sensitivity bands.

result.label: Own-price elasticity, 500ml PET
result.rationale: Mid-size single-serve format; mid-range elasticity.
result.reference: Context only, not a fitted value. Observational elasticities can also differ from experimental ones (https://www.msi.org/working-paper/observational-price-variation-in-scanner-data-cannot-reproduce-experimental-price-elasticities/), so the value carries a range that drives the sensitivity bands.

result.label: Own-price elasticity, 1.5L sharing bottle

result.reference: Context only, not a fitted value. Observational elasticities can also differ from experimental ones (https://www.msi.org/working-paper/observational-price-variation-in-scanner-data-cannot-reproduce-experimental-price-elasticities/), so the value carries a range that drives the sensitivity bands.

Observational elasticities can also differ from experimental ones (https://www.msi.org/working-paper/observational-price-variation-in-scanner-data-cannot-reproduce-experimental-price-elasticities/), so the value carries a range that drives the sensitivity bands.

result.label: Cross-price elasticity, within-brand (different format)
result.rationale: Formats of the same brand substitute for each other more than across brands.
result.reference: Modelling choice; no public source gives brand-pair cross elasticities for this synthetic market. Same caution on observational estimates as the own-price values (https://www.msi.org/working-paper/observational-price-variation-in-scanner-data-cannot-reproduce-experimental-price-elasticities/).

result.label: Cross-price elasticity, across-brand
result.rationale: Weak substitution between competing brands; smaller than within-brand.
result.reference: Modelling choice; no public source gives brand-pair cross elasticities for this synthetic market. Same caution on observational estimates as the own-price values (https://www.msi.org/working-paper/observational-price-variation-in-scanner-data-cannot-reproduce-experimental-price-elasticities/).

result.label: Promo depth saturation rate
result.rationale: Shapes f(depth)=1-exp(-k*depth); k=6 gives strong saturation by 30% depth.
result.reference: Modelling choice. Promotion lift measured against a baseline, with pull-forward and cannibalisation, is standard trade-promotion analytics practice (https://www.tellius.com/cpg/trade-promotion-analytics); the values here are illustrative.

result.label: Promo lift scale (b_promo)
result.rationale: Log-volume lift multiplier applied to the saturating depth curve.
result.reference: Modelling choice. Promotion lift measured against a baseline, with pull-forward and cannibalisation, is standard trade-promotion analytics practice (https://www.tellius.com/cpg/trade-promotion-analytics); the values here are illustrative.

result.label: Promo mechanic multiplier, TPR (temporary price reduction)
result.rationale: Baseline mechanic; no extra lift beyond the depth curve.
result.reference: Modelling choice. Promotion lift measured against a baseline, with pull-forward and cannibalisation, is standard trade-promotion analytics practice (https://www.tellius.com/cpg/trade-promotion-analytics); the values here are illustrative.

result.label: Promo mechanic multiplier, feature & display
result.rationale: In-store visibility adds roughly 25% on top of the depth curve.
result.reference: Modelling choice. Promotion lift measured against a baseline, with pull-forward and cannibalisation, is standard trade-promotion analytics practice (https://www.tellius.com/cpg/trade-promotion-analytics); the values here are illustrative.

result.label: Promo mechanic multiplier, BOGO
result.rationale: BOGO drives the largest lift of the three modelled mechanics.
result.reference: Modelling choice. Promotion lift measured against a baseline, with pull-forward and cannibalisation, is standard trade-promotion analytics practice (https://www.tellius.com/cpg/trade-promotion-analytics); the values here are illustrative.

result.label: Post-promo pull-forward share
result.rationale: 15-25% of a promo's incremental lift is pulled forward from the following week.
result.reference: Modelling choice. Promotion lift measured against a baseline, with pull-forward and cannibalisation, is standard trade-promotion analytics practice (https://www.tellius.com/cpg/trade-promotion-analytics); the values here are illustrative.

recommendations: R1: Prioritise the candidate plan with 500ml PET promotion plus price increases on 1.5L and 6x330ml multipack, as it delivers the highest modeled Aurora gross profit uplift versus baseline (supported by C2, C6, C7, C8, C9, C11, C12, C17).

R2: Where promo flexibility is limited, still execute the price-only move on 1.5L and 6x330ml multipack from the cross-check scenario, which improves Aurora gross profit over baseline though less than the full candidate plan (supported by C3, C8, C9, C13, C18).

R3: Use the candidate architecture with taken price on 1.5L and multipack as the primary lever to defend profit against input-cost shocks, since pure cost increases without pricing or promo changes materially reduce Aurora gross profit (supported by C1, C2, C3, C4, C16).
